clue.text: See 6
Gang leader doing notorious Jack's work (riveting)

indicators.note: the leader of the word gang is its opening letter

parts.note: Jack the Ripper, the notorious Victorian murderer, did his work by ripping

explanation.surface: A crime boss carries on in the manner of a famous killer, and it makes for thrilling reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so absorbing that it holds your attention fast.

clue.text: See 16 across
Any riots in Kabul's new Soviet prison?

indicators.note: one jumble is placed in the middle of the other
a new version of the city name is a rearranged one

parts.note: the Afghan capital's name, the possessive simply tying it to 'new'

indicators.note: letters that riot run wild and fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A question about whether unrest in the Afghan capital has produced a fresh Soviet-style jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'new' works on the city, 'riots' on the first word, and 'in' sets the second jumble after the third letter of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lubyanka was the Moscow headquarters and jail of the KGB, a byword for Soviet detention.

clue.text: A sort of light street dress

parts.note: a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flimsy summer frock to wear out in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashing lamp used in discos and photography is one particular kind of lamp.

clue.text: Raise aloft makeshift nosebag to the Scottish air

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high into the air

indicators.note: something makeshift is improvised, so the letters are thrown together anew

explanation.surface: A horse's feedbag is cobbled together and hoisted up into the Highland breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makeshift' works on nosebag plus 'to' together. 'Air' looks like the sky or breeze, but here it means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Scottish folk tune about Bonnie Prince Charlie's escape, and an air is a melody.

clue.text: Attendant lacks temperature guide

indicators.note: the courtly word goes without one of its letters

parts.note: a courtier attends a monarch at court

explanation.surface: A servant who is short of a thermometer reading is described as a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour courier is the person who escorts and guides travellers on a package holiday.

clue.text: Abroad With Nick, which didn't make the final edit

definitions.text: which didn't make the final edit

parts.note: someone abroad is out of the house or away
to nick is to steal, to take

explanation.surface: A film made overseas with a performer called Nick, in which some footage got cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A filmed shot that is rejected and left out of the finished film or recording.

clue.text: See 22
Old king imprisons spouse, head to foot, in small compartment

indicators.note: the monarch's name locks the other piece up inside it

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: the top letter is sent down to the bottom

parts.note: hubby is a colloquial word for husband

explanation.surface: A tyrant locks up his partner, trussed from top to toe, in a tiny cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to foot' sends the spouse's first letter to the end before 'imprisons' puts the result inside the nursery-rhyme king.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubbyhole is a snug little cupboard or nook for storing things.

clue.text: Lovely to keep a gun as a trinket

indicators.note: the beauty holds the other letters within her

parts.note: a lovely is a beautiful woman, a belle
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman holds on to a firearm as an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a thing of little value or importance, a mere bauble.

clue.text: Quiet leader of India versus a destructive lord

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A low-key Indian prime minister faces a ruinous aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief this god is the destroyer within the trinity of great deities.

clue.text: Track suit top, strapped

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

parts.note: strapped for cash means poor

explanation.surface: An athlete's tracksuit jacket is fastened with a strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track suit' looks like one item of sportswear, but 'Track' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of footprints or droppings left by an animal, which hunters follow.

clue.text: Alloy not encountered in a female, commonly

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for a girl or woman
something unmet has never been come across

explanation.surface: A metal mixture that a woman has, so to speak, never come across.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey bronze of copper and tin once used for casting cannon.

clue.text: A startled demon

parts.note: frit is British dialect for frightened, famously used by Margaret Thatcher

explanation.surface: Something scared appears to be described as a demon.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIT is a northern English dialect word meaning frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabic mythology an afrit is a powerful evil spirit, a kind of jinn.

clue.text: See 6
Good time to cut failed parachute's rubbery substance

indicators.note: the single letter slices into the jumbled word
a failed parachute has collapsed into a different shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word parachute, its 's simply joining it to what follows

explanation.surface: A collapsed parachute leaves a gummy residue, and there is a good moment to slice it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' turns PARACHUTE into UTAPERCHA; 'to cut' puts T after its first letter, giving UTTAPERCHA after G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a latex from Malaysian trees, used for insulating cables and making golf balls.

clue.text: Fool does a turn in Fame — this list should explain

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the other

parts.note: glory is renown or fame

indicators.note: the word performs a turnaround, running backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A clown performs a turn in a show called Fame, and some printed list will make sense of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings, usually at the back of a book.

clue.text: Which could make Bruno have passionate feelings

indicators.note: the clue asks what instruction would produce the name, so the answer is read as wordplay rather than built from the clue

parts.note: a word for scorch, joined by ... (O, the tennis zero) and then mixed, spells this man's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks what might turn a man named Bruno into a smouldering lover.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love is zero, so O; the first word with an O added, rearranged, gives the name in the clue, while the whole phrase also means to feel ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be consumed by ardour or desire for someone, an idiom for intense romantic longing.

clue.text: Puffed out, naff outburst during session

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a bout is a session or spell of activity

indicators.note: an outburst blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone, out of breath, lets slip a rude expletive in the middle of a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naff' is British slang for tacky or uncool; 'outburst' jumbles it and 'during' places it inside the session word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouffant hairstyle is backcombed so that it stands out with volume.

clue.text: Bird Ridge, at this point, is on left

parts.note: a brow is the ridge at the top of a hill
now means at this moment

explanation.surface: A person named Bird, standing on a hill crest, is now positioned on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' and 'Ridge' read as names, but Bird is the definition. A Brown Owl is also the leader of a Brownie pack in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawny owl is also known by this name, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Heat of battle over short period of time

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits over the next

parts.note: a war is a battle on a grand scale

indicators.note: the word for the period is cut down to its abbreviated form

parts.note: a month is a period of time

explanation.surface: The intensity of fighting is said to be spent after a brief interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a moderate degree of hotness, or by extension cordial feeling.

clue.text: Source of nut production

indicators.note: the letters are produced in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The origin of how nuts are grown and harvested.
explanation.definitionFit: A fount is a spring or fountain, and figuratively an origin from which something flows.

clue.text: Sound measure

definitions.meaning: to sound water is to measure its depth, to get to the bottom of it
a unit of six feet used for the depth of water

explanation.surface: A reliable gauge of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to plumb the depth; as a noun it is a nautical unit of length.

clue.text: Watch parts (energy in the winding) on which hours might be recorded

definitions.text: on which hours might be recorded

parts.note: the works are the inner mechanism of a watch

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the twisted word
a winding word is twisted round into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A watch's mechanism, with power fed into the spring as it is wound, records the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' turns THE into HET; 'in' places E inside it, making HEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A worksheet is a form for logging tasks and the time spent on them.

clue.text: See 17 across
Dot's satisfied, getting back a lot of money

definitions.note: read as 'dot is', the 's being a link to the rest

parts.note: a satisfied diner is full

indicators.note: the word for money comes backwards

parts.note: pots of money means a large amount

explanation.surface: A woman called Dot is content, having recovered a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name, but it is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The point ending a sentence is called a dot or period as well.

clue.text: See 17 across
Standing figure guarding king

indicators.note: the sculpture keeps the royal letter safe inside it

parts.note: a statue is a carved figure
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sculpted figure on its plinth stands watch over a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean reputation or importance gained through achievement.

clue.text: Old fellow welcomes backing in new scheme

indicators.note: the old fellow takes the other letters into his midst

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man

indicators.note: the letters are put in reverse

explanation.surface: An elderly man warmly supports a fresh plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses 'in' plus the abbreviation for new together, and 'welcomes' places them after the second letter of the old fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To connive is to plot or conspire secretly, often in wrongdoing.
